div.l: Abought his nek vndre his arme downe
The hote somer made his hewe alle browne
And certeinli he was a gode felawe
Full many a draught of wyne had he drawe
From Burdeux warde whiles þe chapman slepe
Of nyce consciens toke he no kepe
Of þat he fanged and had þe hier hande
Bi water he sent hem home to eueri lande
But of his craft / to reken̄ wel his tides
His stremes and his daunger him bisides
There was none suche fro hull vnto curtage
His herbarowe and his mone his lodemen age
Hardely he was warr and wise to vndertake
With many a tempest was his berde y shake
He knewe al þe hauenes as þei were
Fro gutlond vnto Capifenestre
And eueri cragge in breteyn̄ and in spaine
His barge was cleped þe madalayne
With vs þere was a doctoure of phisik
In al þe world was þere none him like
To speke of phisik and of surgeri
He was grounded in astronomy
He kept his paciens a grete dele
In oure bi magik naturele
Wel couth he fortoune þe Ascendent
Of his Image for his pacient
He knew þe cause of eueri malady
Were it of hete of colde of moist or drie
And were engendered of what homoure
He was a veri ꝑparfit practisoure
The cause he knewe and of his harme þe rote
Anone he gaf þe sike man̄ his bote
Ful redy had he his appoticarys
To send him drages and his lettuaries
For eche of hem made oþer for to wyn̄
Her frendeship was not new to be gyn̄
Wel knew he þe olde Escupalyus
And discordes and eke rusus
Olde Ipocras holi and galiene
Serapioıı̄un rasi and auysene
Auaroys Damascien and constantine
Bernard gattisdene and gilbertyn̄
Of his diete mesurable was he
For it was no suꝑperfluete
